np1-package.def: A bundle of extra Python code you load with import, e.g. import numpy as np.

np1-vectorise.def: Writing an operation on a whole array at once (e.g. 2*x+1) instead of a Python loop over its elements; it runs in compiled code and is much faster.

np1-attribute.def: A fact stored on an object, read with a dot and no brackets: x.shape, x.dtype, x.T.

np1-method.def: A function attached to an object, called with brackets: x.sum(), x.reshape(2, 3).

np1-tuple.def: An ordered sequence in round brackets that cannot be changed, e.g. a shape (2, 3); a one-element tuple is written (5,).

np1-upcast.def: NumPy choosing a more general dtype so that every element fits: one float among integers makes the whole array float64.

np1-slice.def: start:stop:step inside square brackets; picks from start up to but not including stop. Basic slices of arrays are views.

np1-fancy.def: Indexing with a list or integer array, e.g. A[[1, 3]]. Two index lists are paired element by element. Always returns a copy.

np1-mask.def: An array of True/False; x[mask] keeps the elements where it is True. mask.mean() is the fraction of Trues.

np1-scalar.def: A single number (not an array). Arithmetic between an array and a scalar applies the scalar to every element.

np1-reduction.def: An operation that combines many elements into fewer: sum, mean, std, min, max, argmax. With axis=k, axis k disappears.

np1-rowmajor.def: Storing and reshaping an array row by row, so the last index changes fastest (NumPy's default, also called C order).

np1-transpose.def: Swapping rows and columns: element \([i,j]\) moves to \([j,i]\). NumPy A.T, maths \(\mathbf{A}\T\).

np1-view.def: An array that shares memory with another; changing one changes the other. Slices, reshape and .T give views; .copy() makes an independent array.
